# Copilot instructions

## Build and test

- Build the solution: `dotnet build Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.slnx`
- Run the test suite: `dotnet test tests\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.Web.Tests\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.Web.Tests.csproj`
- Run one test: `dotnet test tests\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.Web.Tests\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.Web.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~WorkItemServiceTests.Accept_Hierarchy_CreatesLabelledSubIssuesAndOnlyAssignsTheStory"`
- Restore the local EF tool before using it: `dotnet tool restore`
- Set `ConnectionStrings__Database` in the shell before using EF tools (use the connection string from your local development settings).
- Add a migration: `dotnet ef migrations add <Name> --project src\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.DataAccess.Sql --output-dir Migrations`
- Check the migration snapshot: `dotnet ef migrations has-pending-model-changes --project src\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.DataAccess.Sql`
- Azure deployment: `.github\workflows\release.yml` builds and tests on pushes and pull requests to `main`. On every push to `main`, it applies an EF migrations bundle to Azure SQL and deploys the web app to App Service, `Sync` to the Flex Consumption Function App `softwarefactory-sync` and `Tasks` to `softwarefactory-tasks`; when the `AZURE_CONTAINER_REGISTRY` variable is set, it also builds the `Worker` image on the runner (`src\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.Worker\Dockerfile`, published for `linux-x64` so the Copilot SDK bundles the Linux runtime), pushes it with the registry's admin account (`ACR_USERNAME`/`ACR_PASSWORD` secrets) and, with `AZURE_WORKER_JOB_NAME`, updates the Container Apps job. One-time OIDC setup is in `scripts\setup-azure-github.ps1`; see `docs\azure-deployment.md`.

The app targets .NET 10. Development startup applies EF migrations automatically and uses the LocalDB connection string in `appsettings.Development.json`; other environments must supply `ConnectionStrings:Database`. `appsettings.Development.json` is gitignored, is not published and holds personal settings such as `OpenAI:ApiKey`; `README.md` shows its shape (keep that in sync when adding settings). Development startup migrates whatever database that file points at, so keep it on a local database.
- `SqlServerStoreTests` run against a real SQL Server (a new database per test, built by the migrations): LocalDB on Windows, or the connection string (without database) in `DGHSF_TEST_SQL_SERVER`, which CI sets to a SQL Server service container; they are skipped when neither is available. Use them for what the InMemory provider doesn't enforce (unique indexes, restricted foreign keys, collation, concurrency tokens).
- CI builds with `-p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=true`, so fix analyzer warnings (including in tests) instead of leaving them.

## Architecture

- Project references flow from `Web` to `Application`, and from `Application` to `DataAccess.Sql` and `Agents`. All libraries share `Contracts`, which has no application or infrastructure dependencies. Keep Web free of EF and Agent Framework types.
- `Application/Features` contains MediatR commands, queries, handlers and FluentValidation validators grouped by feature, one type per file in `Commands`, `Queries` and `Validators` subfolders (e.g. `WorkItems/Queries/GetWorkItemQuery.cs` and `GetWorkItemQueryHandler.cs`); these keep the feature namespace. Requests and responses wrap records from `Contracts`; collection responses wrap `CollectionResult<T>`. UI-facing application services dispatch through MediatR, whose validation pipeline runs before handlers and throws `ValidationFailedException` (Contracts). Domain rules that refuse an operation (in stores, workflows and services) throw `DomainRuleException` (Contracts) with a message for the user; UI catch filters show those two (and `PersistenceException`, GitHub errors) and let `InvalidOperationException` surface as a bug. Every request with a repository name validates it with `ValidRepositoryFullName()` (`Application/Common/RepositoryNameRules`), because the name goes into GitHub API URLs.
- `DataAccess.Sql` owns EF entities, DTO mapping, stores, `AppDbContext`, migrations and the design-time factory. Stores live in `Stores` behind interfaces (`IWorkItemStore`, ...) that are registered and injected through DI. Entity configuration lives in `Configuration`, one `ModelBuilder` extension per entity, called from `OnModelCreating`. Stores use `IDbContextFactory<AppDbContext>` and dispose a context per operation. DTOs are separate records, not EF entities. Every entity derives from `Entity`: `Id` (`Guid`, generated by the application) is the nonclustered primary key that foreign keys, contracts and URLs use, and `SysId` (`int` identity) is a clustered alternate key that stays inside `DataAccess.Sql` (`EntityKeysConfiguration`); sort on `SysId` for insertion order, never on `Id`. Existing migration IDs are preserved.
- `Agents` owns Microsoft Agent Framework agents, sessions, streaming and AI form tools. `Application.Features.Assistant` exposes framework-free conversations and tool factories to Web. Contract records are mutable where form binding requires it; use `Copy()` or `with` for editable copies.
- This is a .NET 10 Blazor app using Interactive Server rendering without prerendering for interactive routes. GitHub OAuth is single-user: `Program.cs` enforces the configured allowed login and keeps the access token in the server-side authentication ticket, which `SqlTicketStore` encrypts with data protection and stores in the SQL `AuthSessions` table (through `AuthSessionService`), so sign-ins survive restarts and deployments; the cookie only holds a random session key. GitHub API calls get the token from the `GitHubClaims.AccessToken` claim through `AuthenticationStateProvider`.
- The app operates on one selected repository per Blazor circuit. `RepositoryContext` restores and stores the selection in protected browser local storage, and `MainLayout` then refreshes it from GitHub (`RefreshAsync`; the stored copy is kept when GitHub can't be reached); `MainLayout` requires a selection and keys the page body by repository full name so switching repositories recreates the page. Pages marked `[RepositoryIndependent]` (detected through the `RouteData` cascaded from `Routes.razor`) render without a selection, e.g. the agent template pages.
- Repository selection and restored selections update SQL `RepositoryAccesses` through `RepositoryHistoryService`. The picker loads the five most recent names/access times independently of GitHub's full repository list and fetches a recent repository directly when selected before that list finishes.
- Agent templates (`AgentTemplateService`) are stored in SQL Server as full agent file content, are shared across repositories, and are applied to one or more repositories through the application workflow and `GitHubApiClient`. `AgentEditor` and `AgentTemplateEditor` share the `Components/Shared/AgentForm.razor` form.
- Copilot agent skills (`Skill` in Contracts, `SkillService`/`SkillWorkflow`) are managed globally: the `Skills` table stores their properties (name, description, optional license, compatibility and allowed tools, Markdown instructions), not a file. The name is also the directory name (`Skill.IsValidName`: lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, at most 64 characters; unique). `SkillFileSerializer` turns a skill into `.github/skills/{name}/SKILL.md` (frontmatter in a fixed order, empty optional properties left out). `/skills` (`Skills.razor`, linked right before the agents) lists every skill with a switch for the selected repository: enabling commits the `SKILL.md` directly to the default branch, disabling deletes it (other files in the directory stay). Nothing about enabled skills is stored in SQL: `SkillWorkflow.GetRepositorySkillsAsync` lists the `.github/skills` directories and reads the files of managed skills only, so a skill is Enabled, Disabled or Outdated (the file differs, ignoring line endings; enabling again updates it), and directories without a managed skill are reported as unmanaged. Saving, renaming or deleting a skill doesn't change repositories. `/skills/new` and `/skills/edit/{id}` (`SkillEditor.razor`) are repository independent and show a preview of the `SKILL.md`.
- Repository-backed features should use `RepositoryContext.Current` and pass the repository full name through application service operations. Work items are scoped by repository; the managed AI model catalog, agent templates, skills and work item templates are shared across repositories.
- `Sync` is an isolated-worker Azure Function app that references only `Application` (through `AddSoftwareFactory`). `WorkItemSyncFunction` runs on the CRON expression in the `WorkItemSyncSchedule` app setting and calls `WorkItemSyncService`, which refreshes every item with `WorkItem.HasIssue` (also closed ones, so a reopened issue moves back) of every repository in `IRepositoryStore.GetAllAsync` through `WorkItemService.RefreshAsync`. Nobody is signed in when the timer fires, so its `IGitHubTokenProvider` returns `GitHub:SyncToken` from configuration. A run first lists the eligible items of every repository (database only), then refreshes them one by one in issue order. Transient errors (GitHub 5xx/408, network errors, HttpClient timeouts, database errors) are retried per item after `WorkItemSyncOptions.RetryDelays` (tests set them to zero); any other error of one item or repository, also an unexpected one, is reported in `WorkItemSyncResult` and doesn't stop the others. Only a refused token or reached rate limit (and cancellation) stops the run and throws, because every other request would fail too. `WorkItemRefreshResult.ProgressWarning` says when Copilot's progress couldn't be read (no access to pull requests, or to Actions: `GitHubApiClient.GetLatestCopilotRunAsync` returns `CopilotRunLookup.CanReadActions`). `local.settings.json` is gitignored; `README.md` shows its shape.
- The sync writes what it did to the `SyncLogEvents` table (`ISyncLogStore`, kept forever, no foreign keys) and to `ILogger`: per run one event per changed item (`WorkItemChanges.Describe`), per failed item or repository, one `ProgressUnavailable` warning per repository and reason, and a `RunCompleted` summary; a stopped or cancelled run logs how far it got. A run without changes or problems doesn't write those: consecutive `NoChanges` runs, and consecutive `NoEligibleWorkItems` runs ("No action for {x} iterations because no work items are in an eligible state"), each share one event whose `Iterations` counts them (`ISyncLogStore.AddOrRepeatAsync` repeats the newest event when it has the same kind). Writing the log never fails the sync. `/sync-log` (`SyncLog.razor`, repository independent) shows the events newest first (`LastOccurredAt`, then `SysId`) with server-side paging through `SyncLogService` (MediatR `GetSyncLogQuery`, `PagedResult<T>`), filtered on level and up and on repository; only the sync writes the table.
- `Tasks` is a second isolated-worker Function app (also only `Application`, `GitHub:TasksToken` through `ConfiguredGitHubTokenProvider`) that executes **background tasks**: rows in `TodoTasks` (`ITodoTaskStore`, no foreign keys; a run is a tree with `RootId`/`ParentId`). The SQL table is the source of truth and Service Bus only carries task ids. `TodoTaskDispatcher` (timer `TodoTaskDispatch`, `[ServiceBusOutput]`) recovers stuck tasks and claims due `Pending` tasks as `Queued`. `TodoTaskExecutor` (queue trigger `TodoTaskExecute`) claims `Queued` → `Running` with a lease, runs the `ITodoTaskHandler` of the task's `TodoTaskKind`, and stores the result plus the sub-tasks (the parent becomes `Waiting` and ends with its last sub-task). Every status change is a conditional `ExecuteUpdateAsync` on the expected status, so duplicate messages and concurrent dispatchers are harmless. Retries go through the database (`NotBefore`, `TodoTaskOptions`), never through redelivery. A `DomainRuleException` fails a task without retrying. Handlers must be safe to re-run (they skip titles that already exist). The web app only creates runs and reads them through `TodoTaskService`; `/background-tasks` (`BackgroundTasks.razor`) shows them. The first kinds are `AnalyzeRepository` and `WriteFeatureWorkItems` (`Features/RepositoryAnalysis`): the Repository Analyst and Repository Work Item Writer internal agents read the repository with `RepositoryExplorerTools` (a read budget per agent) through `RepositoryFiles`: with `RepositorySnapshots` configured, the first task of a run downloads the tarball once (`GitHubApiClient.DownloadTarballAsync`) and stores the files `RepositoryTreeFilter` keeps in a private blob container under the run id (`IRepositorySnapshotStorage`, deleted by `RepositorySnapshotCleaner` once the run has ended); without it, `GetTreeAsync` and `GetFileAsync` per task and save drafts tagged with `WorkItem.GeneratedByTaskId` (the root task), which `IWorkItemStore.DeleteGeneratedDraftsAsync` can discard.
- **Agent worker**: a story, bug or task has an `AgentExecutor` (`WorkItem.Executor`, stored as a number, reset to `CopilotCloudAgent` for epics and features): the Copilot cloud agent, or `DghsfWorker`. For the worker, `WorkItemWorkflow.TryAssignAsync` assigns nobody on GitHub but adds an `AgentRuns` row (`IAgentRunStore`, `Contracts.AgentRuns`, no foreign keys, status by name: Pending → Queued → Running → Succeeded/Failed/Cancelled; refused while the item has a run that hasn't ended) and marks the item assigned. Like the background tasks, SQL is the source of truth and every status change is a conditional `ExecuteUpdateAsync` on the expected status. `AgentRunDispatcher` (Tasks function `AgentRunDispatch`, on `TodoTaskDispatchSchedule`; does nothing without `AgentRuns:QueueName`) recovers stuck runs and sends the ids of pending runs to the queue with the Service Bus SDK (`AgentRunQueue`, the same `ServiceBus` connection settings as the Functions extension), not with an output binding. `Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.Worker` is a console app (references `Application` and `GitHub.Copilot.SDK`; only it does, because the package copies the Copilot runtime into every referencing project's output) for an event-driven Container Apps job: `AgentRunWorker` receives one message, `TryStartAsync` claims the run with a lease, the message is completed at once (an agent works far longer than a Service Bus lock lasts), and `AgentRunExecutor` renews the lease every third of `AgentRunOptions.Lease`; a failed renewal means the run was cancelled, which stops the agent without pushing. The executor clones the base branch (`IGitWorkspace`/`GitWorkspace`: the token goes to git through `GIT_CONFIG_*` environment variables of the clone and push only), runs `ICodingAgent` (`CopilotCodingAgent`: every tool approved, `AgentRunPrompt.Instructions` appended to the system prompt, the custom agent read from the clone, optional `SessionLimits`, the runtime started with `AgentEnvironment.Sanitized` so the agent's shell never sees the worker's secrets), commits and pushes the branch (`AgentRunPrompt.BranchName`), opens the pull request (`GitHubApiClient.CreatePullRequestAsync`, `Closes #n`; a draft when the agent stopped early, which `AgentRun.Error` then explains on a succeeded run) and stores the session's usage (`session.Rpc.Usage.GetMetricsAsync`: nano AI units, 10⁹ per AI credit, plus tokens and models). Only a failure before the agent started is retried (`AgentRunOptions.MaxAttempts`); afterwards a retry would pay for the agent again, so the user starts another run (`StartAgentRunCommand`, Run again). Refreshing a worker item (`RefreshFromIssueAsync`) treats it as assigned while it has a run that wasn't cancelled and takes its progress from `CopilotProgressEvaluator.EvaluateWorker` (the latest run until it succeeded, then the linked pull request; no Actions lookup). The editor's assignment box has a Runs on select, and `AgentRunsPanel` (Shared) lists the runs with their AI credits. `/background-tasks` also shows the repository's latest runs (`GetRepositoryAgentRunsQuery`, `AgentRunOverview` with the work item, which is `null` for a deleted one) with their total cost and a Cancel run button, and keeps reloading while one is active. `docs/azure-deployment.md` describes the job.
- Work items (epics, features, user stories, bugs and tasks) share one model: `WorkItem` with a `WorkItemType`, stored in the `WorkItems` table with a self-referencing `ParentId`; templates are `WorkItemTemplate` rows per type. `WorkItemTypeRules` (Contracts) holds the label, label color, names and hierarchy per type: a feature needs an epic parent, a story needs a feature parent, bugs and tasks are standalone or part of an epic, feature or story. Only stories, bugs and tasks are assigned to the Copilot cloud agent; the store clears assignment settings for epics and features. `WorkItemStore` enforces the hierarchy and refuses to delete items with children. `WorkItemWorkflow` creates the labelled issue (creating the label when missing), makes it a sub-issue of the parent's issue and makes the issues of already accepted children its sub-issues (the sub-issues API needs GitHub's issue id, stored as `IssueId`). Accepting first claims the draft (`AcceptStartedAt`, a concurrency token like `Status`; a claim expires after `WorkItemWorkflow.AcceptClaimTimeout`) so concurrent accepts can't both create an issue. When an attempt failed after GitHub may have created the issue (not for a 4xx refusal), `AcceptIssueSince` remembers when it started and the next attempt first looks for the issue with the item's marker among the label's issues updated since then (`FindIssueByMarkerAsync`), reusing it instead of creating a duplicate. The marker (`WorkItemWorkflow.Marker`, `<!-- dghsf:label:id:created-ms -->`) includes the creation time, so items of different databases never share one. Below the description, the issue body lists the issues of the whole hierarchy above the item (`WorkItemWorkflow.ParentIssuesSection`: `### Parent issues`, then `- {Type}: #{number}` from the top down to the direct parent; only the bare reference, because GitHub renders it with the issue's state icon and title: an added title shows twice, and a link with its own text loses the icon and title), so the Copilot cloud agent has them as context; it sits between the hidden `<!-- dghsf:parents -->` and `<!-- dghsf:parents:end -->` markers, so `RefreshFromIssueAsync` leaves it out of the stored description. Optional `WorkItem.TechnicalDetails` (Markdown, edited below the description while the item is a draft; the work item chat agent fills it from the chat and from the parents' technical details: every request lists which parents in the whole hierarchy have them, and `get_parent_technical_details` reads them through `WorkItemService.GetAncestorsAsync`, closest parent first, for the parent currently on the form) stays out of the issue body: within the same claimed attempt, right after the issue exists and before the item is marked accepted or assigned to Copilot, it is posted as the issue's first comment under `WorkItemWorkflow.TechnicalDetailsHeading` with its own marker (`TechnicalDetailsMarker`). A failure to post it fails the attempt, and a retry that reuses the issue first checks its comments for that marker. Refreshing from GitHub never changes it.
- Accepted items (`WorkItem.HasIssue`) have a Refresh from GitHub button on the list and on the editor. `WorkItemWorkflow.RefreshFromIssueAsync` (MediatR `RefreshWorkItemCommand`) reads the issue and `IWorkItemStore.ApplyIssueAsync` stores its title, body without the marker, id and URL, and the status that follows from it: closed is Done (labeled Closed in the UI); open is In progress when Copilot is assigned (only for assignable types), otherwise Accepted. So a reopened or unassigned issue moves back. It only reads from GitHub, `UpdatedAt` changes only when something differed, and the editor keeps unsaved assignment settings.
- The work item pages (`WorkItems`, `WorkItemEditor`, `WorkItemTemplates`, `WorkItemTemplateEditor`) each serve all types through one `@page` per type; `WorkItemRoutes` maps types to URLs (`/epics`, `/features`, `/stories`, `/bugs`, `/tasks`, `/{label}-templates`) and reads the type from the URL. The pages take the cascaded `RouteData` so navigating between types (same component) reloads them. That cascade reaches the current page before its own parameters are updated, so a page combining the URL's type with its `Id` first checks `WorkItemRoutes.IsOutOfStep`; without that check it sees the new URL with the old id.
- The overview page shows `RepositoryInfographic` (Shared): whether the Copilot instructions file exists, the number of custom agents (from the directory listing with `AgentCatalog.IsAgentFile`, without reading every file) and, in the same box split in two halves, the number of skills (the directories in `.github/skills`, also from the listing alone) and per work item type the `WorkItemCounts` from one `GROUP BY` in `IWorkItemStore.GetCountsAsync`. The counts are by current status, so every item is in exactly one: draft, accepted (Accepted or In progress) or closed (Done). Each part fails on its own, so GitHub being unreachable doesn't hide the counts.
- Below it, `CopilotActivityInfographic` and `CopilotBillingInfographic` (Shared) show live GitHub data; nothing is stored in SQL. Activity: the selected repository's Copilot pull request activity over the last 28 days, from GitHub's Copilot usage metrics `orgs/{org}/copilot/metrics/reports/repos-1-day` report (only for organization-owned repositories, `GitHubOwner.IsOrganization`; needs an organization owner or the View Organization Copilot Metrics permission, the usage metrics policy and the `read:org` OAuth scope). There is no multi-day repository report, so `GetCopilotRepositoryMetricsQueryHandler` requests one report per day (4 at a time). Each report returns signed links to NDJSON files, which `GitHubApiClient` downloads **without** the GitHub token, and the handler caches each day's rows per organization in `IMemoryCache`. A 404 for one of the last 3 days counts as not published yet; an older 404 is an access problem. GitHub has no usage metrics for personal accounts, so for a personal repository `GetCopilotPullRequestActivityQueryHandler` works out the same period from the pull requests list (sorted by update time, so paging stops at the first one updated before the period) and each pull request's reviews. Authors and reviewers are Copilot when `GitHubOwner.IsCopilot` (a Bot whose login contains "copilot"), and each pull request counts once, on the day of its first Copilot review. It sets `CopilotRepositoryMetrics.FromPullRequests`; then the component hides the review comment stat and severity table and says where the numbers come from. The result is cached for 10 minutes per repository. Don't use the search API for this: its secondary rate limit trips after a few quick requests. Billing: this month's (UTC) premium request and AI credit usage of the repository owner (`organizations/{org}/...` or `users/{login}/settings/billing/{premium_request|ai_credit}/usage`), per model. The user endpoints only accept the full `user` OAuth scope (hence `user` instead of `read:user` at sign-in) and answer 404 without it; the organization endpoints accept `repo` and need an organization owner or billing manager. The two reports fail independently. Billing amounts are shown in US dollars, as GitHub bills them, not with `AiModel.FormatPrice`. These endpoints are sent with `X-GitHub-Api-Version` `GitHubApiClient.UsageApiVersion`; the rest of the client keeps the default version.
- Custom agent profiles live in each repository's `.github/agents` directory and are read or committed through `GitHubApiClient`. `AgentFileSerializer` preserves unedited YAML frontmatter keys and their order; retain that behavior when changing agent-file editing.
- `/copilot-instructions` (`CopilotInstructions.razor`) edits the selected repository's `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (`CopilotInstructionsFile` in Contracts) in `MarkdownEditor` and commits it directly to the default branch through `GitHubService.PutFileAsync` (no sha when the file doesn't exist yet). Its Copilot (`CopilotInstructionsFormTools`) can list and read repository files (read-only, long files are cut off) to write concrete instructions, and replaces the editor content; the user saves.
- `/copilot-code-review` (`CopilotCodeReview.razor`) reads and changes the selected repository's Copilot code review settings live through `repos/{owner}/{repo}/copilot/code-review/settings`; nothing is stored in SQL. Every control sends a `PATCH` with only its own setting and shows the settings GitHub returns. GitHub's API offers review effort, severity filter, custom instructions and MCP, but not maximum review effort or approvals, and requires repository administrator access.
- `/work-item-map` (`WorkItemMap.razor`, linked right after the overview) shows all work items of the selected repository as a mind map from one `WorkItemService.GetAllAsync`. `WorkItemMapLayout` (Shared, pure C#, unit tested) computes it: one expanded epic in the middle with its descendants on elliptical rings per depth (each subtree gets an angle proportional to its leaves), or, with `?epic=all`, the repository hub with the epics around it and the bugs and tasks without a parent on an outer ring. `?epic={id}` picks the expanded epic; without it the first open epic alphabetically is expanded. Expanding an epic (from the dock of all epics at the bottom, or the badge on an epic around the hub) replaces the previous one and updates the URL with `replace`. Every node links to its detail page. Positions are percentages of the map area; the lines are one SVG with `viewBox="0 0 100 100"`, `preserveAspectRatio="none"` and non-scaling strokes. The animations are CSS only (`WorkItemMap.razor.css`): new nodes grow from their parent's position (`--fx`/`--fy`), and epics keep their `@key` between the hub and the middle so they glide there. The layout fits the items to the map's real size in pixels: `WorkItemMap.razor.js` reports the stage size through a `ResizeObserver` (debounced) to the `[JSInvokable] Resize`, which lays the map out again (until then `WorkItemMapLayout.DefaultWidth`/`DefaultHeight`). Each node takes a box (badge plus label below it, the sizes in `WorkItemMapLayout.Box`, which must match `WorkItemMap.razor.css`), and the rings are fitted from the inside out so no boxes overlap: tree angles are warped so equal steps get equal room on the ellipse, every node picks its own radius, a full ring staggers every other node, the ring's nodes shrink (`Scale`, down to `MinScale`, the CSS `--scale`), and only nodes that still don't fit are `Crowded` and show their labels on hover or focus only. Rings with room spread out to the full map at full size. While an epic is expanded, a strip above the map (`ProgressHeight`, left out of the map's room like the dock's `DockHeight`) shows `WorkItemMapLayout.Progress`: the percentage of the items below the epic that are closed, and a stacked bar of closed, accepted (including in progress, as on the overview) and draft items.
- `/mindmaps` (`MindmapOverview.razor`, linked right after the overview) shows the selected repository's mindmaps as cards (title, done progress, last update; most recently updated first) plus a New card, and still opens the old address `/mindmaps?id=…&idea=…` of a map. `/mindmaps/{id}` and `/mindmaps/new` (`Mindmaps.razor`; URLs in `MindmapRoutes`) edit one mindmap: simple to-do lists with one central idea (the only `MindmapNode` without a `ParentId`) and ideas below it, each with a text and a done flag. A mindmap (`Mindmap` in Contracts, `MindmapService`, `IMindmapStore`) is stored as one `Mindmaps` row with its ideas as a JSON array in `Nodes` (the stored shape is `MindmapStore.NodeData`; keep its property names) and a copy of the central idea in `Title` for the list; it's always saved as a whole. `SaveMindmapValidator` refuses anything that isn't one tree (`Mindmap.StructureProblem`), empty or too long texts and more than `Mindmap.MaxNodes` ideas. Positions are pixels relative to the central idea. The editor's title is a button that opens the quick switcher (`MindmapSwitcherDialog`, Shared; also Ctrl+K / ⌘K through `Mindmaps.razor.js` and the `[JSInvokable] OpenSwitcherFromBrowser`): filter by title, arrow keys and Enter to open another map or start a new one. The editor has Save and Reset like other editors, with a `NavigationLock` against losing unsaved changes. `MindmapLayout` (Shared, pure C#, unit tested) places new ideas (around the centre right and left first, further out in the direction of the parent, at the first place that doesn't overlap another idea; the sizes must match `Mindmaps.razor.css`), moves an idea with everything below it, moves it below another idea (placing that branch again, never below itself) and removes it with everything below it (never the central idea). Dragging is done by `Mindmaps.razor.js` without a round trip per mouse move: it only sets the `translate` style of the moving ideas and lines (and draws the line to the parent on the spare `.mindmap-drag-edge` path), then calls the `[JSInvokable] Move` with the distance or the idea it was dropped on; after rendering the new positions the page calls `settle`, which removes those styles so whatever Blazor rendered shows. Ideas are edited in place: a click selects (`Select`) and shows a row of buttons below the idea (edit, add an idea below, done, remove), a second click on the same idea within 400 ms edits it (`EditFromBrowser`; the browser's own `dblclick` is unreliable with pointer capture), and so do Enter or F2 on a focused idea. In the inline input Enter commits, Escape cancels, Tab commits and adds an idea below, and an empty text keeps the old one; new ideas (and the central idea of a new map) start in edit mode. Dragging the background pans (not stored). Ideas are `width: max-content` because the world element has no width.
- Mindmap ideas can be linked to a work item of the same repository (`MindmapNode.WorkItemId`, in the JSON; one item per idea, an item may be linked from several ideas). A linked idea shows a badge with the item's type icon and issue number or status, linking to the item (a missing item shows a broken link). The selected idea's work item button is a `MudMenu`: open the item, link an existing item (`LinkWorkItemDialog`, Shared: search plus type filter, items most like the idea first), unlink, or create a new epic, feature, story, bug or task from the idea. Linking on the page is an edit of the map (saved with Save). Creating saves the map first and opens the editor at `WorkItemRoutes.NewPath(type, parent, mindmapId, ideaId)` (`?mindmap=&idea=`); the parent is `MindmapLayout.ProposedParent`, the item of the nearest idea above that can contain the type. The editor then shows where the item comes from and lets the Mindmap Work Item Writer background agent (`GenerateMindmapWorkItemQuery`, `BackgroundAgents.WriteMindmapWorkItemAsync`) write the title and description from the whole map as an outline (`BackgroundAgents.MindmapOutline`: the chosen idea marked, done and linked ideas annotated), the selected template and the parent; Write again replaces them. Without the agent (disabled, unconfigured or failing) the idea becomes the title and the template the description. `SaveCoreAsync` links the new item to the idea (`LinkMindmapIdeaCommand`, which changes only that idea). A stored item shows a chip per linked idea next to its type (`IMindmapStore.GetLinkedIdeasAsync`, `GetLinkedMindmapIdeasQuery`) that opens `/mindmaps/{map}?idea={idea}`; the mindmap page selects an idea from `?idea=` once and pans it to the middle (`centerOn` in `Mindmaps.razor.js`). Ideas linked to a closed item are done: `RefreshWorkItemCommandHandler` (the Refresh button and the sync) calls `IMindmapStore.MarkWorkItemDoneAsync` when the item is Done (failures are logged, never fail the refresh), `LinkMindmapIdeaCommand` and `SaveMindmapCommandHandler` mark ideas of closed items done, and the page shows them done on load. Reopening an item doesn't undo it.
- `/knowledge-base` (`KnowledgeBase.razor`, repository independent, linked right after the work item map) is a library of files in virtual folders (`KnowledgeBaseService`, `IKnowledgeBaseStore`, `Features/KnowledgeBase`). A file is global (`KnowledgeFile.RepositoryFullName` null) or belongs to one repository (`KnowledgeFiles.RepositoryId`, restricted foreign key), chosen with the Global checkbox in `KnowledgeFileDialog` (unchecked links it to the selected repository; without a selection only global is possible). Folders always belong to one repository (`KnowledgeFolders.RepositoryId`, required; a folder never changes repository, its parent is in the same repository, names are unique per repository and parent) and only hold that repository's files: a global file is never in a folder (validators and the store refuse it), so the dialog hides the folder picker while Global is checked and saves global files at the top. `IKnowledgeBaseStore.GetLibraryAsync(repository)` returns the global files and that repository's folders and files (no folders without a repository), which is what the page and `KnowledgeFilePickerDialog` show; `GetFullLibraryAsync` (all repositories) is only for blob metadata paths. The table shows a Global group (only at the top of the library, and in search results) and then the repository's group with its folders and files, each under its own header row (`Row.Group`); inside a folder only the repository's group. New folder needs a selected repository. Migration `AddKnowledgeFolderRepository` assigned existing folders the repository of the files in or around them, moved global files out of folders and deleted folders left without a repository. Folders (`KnowledgeFolders`: self-referencing `ParentId`, name unique per parent through an unfiltered unique index, so also at the top) and file metadata (`KnowledgeFiles`: title, description, folder, original file name, content type, size) are in SQL; folders exist only there. Each file's content is a blob named after its `Id` (`AzureBlobKnowledgeFileStorage.BlobName`) in its own public container (`KnowledgeBase` config section, `KnowledgeBaseOptions`; blob read access, not listing, created on first upload). `UploadKnowledgeFileCommandHandler` picks the id, streams the content to the blob and then adds the row, deleting the blob again when that fails; deleting removes the row first and then the blob (a failure is only logged). The content can't be replaced, so a link never changes and blobs are cached as immutable; editing changes only title, description and folder. Each blob also carries the `title`, `description` and virtual `path` (`/Specs/API`, `/` at the top; `KnowledgeFileMetadata`) as blob metadata, percent-encoded UTF-8 because metadata must be ASCII, and shortened with an ellipsis to stay within Azure's 8 KB per blob (`AzureBlobKnowledgeFileStorage.ToBlobMetadata`; an empty description is left out), plus `scope` (`global` or `repository`) and, for a repository's file, `repository` (lowercase `owner/name`), both unencoded because Azure AI Search copies them as they are to each passage to filter on. Uploading sets it; editing a file, and renaming or moving a folder (for every file below it), rewrites it through `KnowledgeFileMetadataSync` after the database change, which stays the source of truth: a failed metadata update is logged and doesn't fail the save. Because Azure returns metadata as `x-ms-meta-*` headers on anonymous downloads, the title, description and path are as public as the file: the page and `KnowledgeFileDialog` (upload and edit) show `KnowledgeBaseRoutes.PublicNotice`, a warning not to store confidential data; keep it there and keep confidential details out of anything this feature makes public. Blobs carry a `Content-Disposition` with the original file name, `attachment` for active types (HTML, SVG, XML, JavaScript) and `inline` otherwise. The store refuses duplicate folder names, moving a folder below itself and deleting a folder that still has folders or files. `GetKnowledgeLibraryQuery` returns every folder and file at once (`KnowledgeLibrary`, with path helpers) with each file's public `Url`; the page browses folders with `?folder={id}` (folder trail in `PageBreadcrumbs`) and searches all files client-side. Work items link to files through `MarkdownEditor.AllowFileLinks` (description and technical details in `WorkItemEditor`): a toolbar button added in `MarkdownEditor.razor.js` calls the `[JSInvokable] PickFileLink`, which opens `KnowledgeFilePickerDialog` and returns the title and URL that Toast UI's `addLink` command inserts.
- Knowledge base search (RAG): with the `KnowledgeSearch` config section (`KnowledgeSearchOptions`: endpoint, query key, index name, optional semantic configuration, `MaxResults`), the work item chat agents get `search_knowledge_base` (`WorkItemFormTools`, passed in by `WorkItemEditor` through `AssistantForms.ForWorkItem`; left out when unconfigured, and the default prompt only mentions it conditionally). An Azure AI Search indexer (definitions in `docs/knowledge-base-search`, created by `scripts/setup-knowledge-search.ps1`; nothing in DGHSF writes to the index) splits each blob into passages, embeds them with Azure OpenAI and stores one document per passage with `file_id` (the blob name), `chunk`, `text_vector`, `scope` and `repository`; keep those field names in sync with `AzureAiKnowledgeSearchIndex`. `IKnowledgeSearchIndex` runs a hybrid query (keywords plus a `VectorizableTextQuery` that the index's vectorizer embeds) filtered on `scope eq 'global' or scope eq null or repository eq '{repo}'` (built with `SearchFilter.Create`, which escapes the values). `SearchKnowledgeBaseQueryHandler` then keeps only passages of files the database still shows for that repository (the index lags behind and doesn't see deletions until the indexer runs) and takes title, link and folder from the database. Blob names have no extension, so the indexer must not filter on file extensions.
- `/actions` (`Actions.razor`, linked after the knowledge base) shows the selected repository's GitHub Actions workflows (`GetWorkflowsQuery`, all pages, by name, including GitHub's dynamic ones such as Copilot's agent) and their runs newest first, live from GitHub; nothing is stored in SQL. Picking a workflow in the list filters the runs (`repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/{id}/runs`, otherwise `actions/runs`). The runs table pages on the server (`GetWorkflowRunsQuery`, `WorkflowRunsRequest`, at most 100 per page, GitHub's `total_count`). A run's duration is from `run_started_at` to `updated_at` of a completed run, because the runs list has no completion time. The workflows and the runs fail independently. `?workflow={id}` preselects a workflow. Run states, colors, icons and durations come from `WorkflowRunDisplay` (Shared). On the overview, `WorkflowRunsInfographic` (Shared, just above `CopilotSessionsInfographic`) shows every workflow's latest run (`GetLatestWorkflowRunsQuery`: the workflows, then one `per_page=1` runs request per workflow, 4 at a time, because the newest runs of the repository can all belong to one busy workflow), most recently run first and workflows that never ran last; each workflow links to `/actions?workflow={id}`.
- DGHSF's internal agents use the singleton `AssistantAgentFactory` in `Agents` and the `OpenAI` config section (`Endpoint`, `Model`, `ApiKey`; unconfigured means the chat shows a setup hint). The fixed set of agents and their default system prompts live in `InternalAgentDefaults` (keys in Contracts `InternalAgentKeys`): one chat agent (kind `Copilot`, formerly called Copilots; keys and enum names keep that name because they are stored) per work item type, per work item template type, for agents, for agent templates, for the Copilot instructions file and for skills (Copilot Skills Agent, `SkillFormTools`; its chat is not stored), plus the background agents Model Selector, Chat Suggestions, Description Writer, Work Item Breakdown and Mindmap Work Item Writer. They are stored in the `InternalAgents` table (seeded at startup through `SeedApplicationDataAsync` and whenever the list is loaded; seeding adds missing agents and refreshes name/description but keeps edited prompts and the enabled flag). `InternalAgentRegistry` merges the stored prompt with the defaults; `/internal-agents` edits the prompt, enables/disables and resets an agent. Internal agents are global, not per repository. Every internal agent links to a row of the internal model catalog (`InternalModel`, `/internal-models`: the Microsoft Foundry model or deployment name that is sent to the endpoint, a required one-line `Label` shown when choosing a model, a longer description and EUR per 1M input/output tokens, plus an optional cached input price that falls back to the input price; unrelated to the GitHub-facing `AiModel` catalog), chosen in a select (`AssistantAgentFactory` creates a client per model). A model can be marked `IsFlagship` (any number) and `IsDefault` (at most one, because `InternalModelStore.SaveAsync` clears the previous default in the same save). Seeding links newly added agents to the default model and leaves existing ones alone. An agent without a link uses `OpenAI:Model`. The editor prefills a chat agent's empty model with the default model, or else the catalog entry named like `OpenAI:Model`, prefills a background agent's empty model with the default until that agent is first saved, requires a model for chat agents (optional for background agents) and only enables Save once a new or changed model has passed its Test (`InternalAgentService.TestModelAsync` sends a real request). Resetting restores only the prompt. A model in use can't be deleted.
- `/chat` (`Chat.razor`, linked right after the overview; also `/chat/{id}`, URLs in `ChatRoutes`) is a chat with the DGHSF Agent (`InternalAgentKeys.DghsfAgent`, a chat agent like the Copilots, usage source `DghsfAgentChat`) about the whole project of the selected repository, with the repository's conversations on the left, most recently used first. A conversation (`ProjectChat` in Contracts, `ProjectChatService`, `IProjectChatStore`, `Features/ProjectChats`) is a `ProjectChats` row (repository, title, `CreatedAt`, `LastUsedAt`; restricted foreign key to the repository) with its `ProjectChatMessages` (stored like `ChatMessages`: display text and replayed payload per message, so tool calls are replayed); unlike the editors' `ChatConversations` a repository has any number of them and none is closed. The first message starts the row, titled after the message (`ProjectChatService.FallbackTitle`), and the page navigates to its address with `replace`; meanwhile the Chat Title Writer background agent (`InternalAgentKeys.ChatTitleWriter`, `BackgroundAgents.WriteChatTitleAsync`, usage source `ChatTitleWriter`) renames it in two words (`CleanChatTitle`); when it is disabled or fails, the conversation keeps the fallback title. Every finished exchange is appended and moves the conversation to the top. Every `ProjectChat.SummaryInterval` (10) chat messages (rows with display text: the user's messages and the replies) the page lets the Chat Summarizer background agent (`InternalAgentKeys.ChatSummarizer`, `ProjectConversation.SummarizeIfDueAsync` in the background, `SummarizeProjectChatCommand`, `BackgroundAgents.SummarizeChatAsync`) merge the last summary with the messages after it. The summary is stored as a `ProjectChatMessages` row with `IsSummary` (its text in `DisplayText`, a system message from `AssistantConversation.SummaryPayload` as payload) and every row it covers gets `IsSummarized`; `GetPayloadsAsync` replays the last summary and then the rows without `IsSummarized` (by the flag, not the position, so an exchange stored while the summary was written stays in), the chat shows every message but no summary, and the open conversation restores from the summary before its next message. Summarizing and appending are serialized per conversation; without a model, with the agent disabled or when it fails, nothing is summarized and a later exchange tries again. The agent is read-only: `ProjectAgentTools` (Agents) reads work items (outline, search, details), mindmaps, the knowledge base (and `search_knowledge_base` when configured), work item templates, skills, background task runs and the sync log through `IProjectAgentData`, implemented by `ProjectAgentData` over the application services (so every read is validated and scoped to the repository); `RepositoryFileTools` (shared with `CopilotInstructionsFormTools`) lists and reads files, and the page connects the GitHub MCP tools pinned to the repository (the first message waits for that connection). `ChatLog` (Shared) renders the messages for both `AssistantChat` and the chat page. Like `AssistantChat`, the input's Send adornment is a microphone while the input is empty (with Azure AI Speech, `SpeechDictation.ListenOnceAsync`): what is said fills the input, to send with Enter.
- All prices and costs are shown in euro with 3 decimals through `AiModel.FormatPrice`. That is display only: more decimals are stored and used to calculate, and `ModelPricingScraper` copies GitHub's US dollar amounts without converting them.
- Token spend: `UsageTrackingChatClient` sits below the agent's function invocation loop, so every model request (each round trip of a tool-using turn, streaming or not) reports its `UsageDetails` through `IAgentUsageRecorder`; so does a model Test on the editor, which counts towards that agent at the price of the tested model. `IInternalAgentStore.RecordUsageAsync` prices the request from the catalog at that moment and, in one save, adds an `InternalAgentUsages` row (a copy of the model name, prices and costs, no foreign key to the model) and adds to the running totals on `InternalAgents`, so later price changes don't affect past costs. Reasoning tokens are stored and shown for information only: they are part of the output tokens and already in the output cost, so never charge them separately. Every row has an `InternalAgentUsageSource` (an enum with descriptions, stored by name): the background agents and the model Test pass their own, and `InternalAgentUsageSources.ForCopilot` maps a Copilot's key to its chat, so a new agent needs a new member there. `UsageTiles` and `UsageRequestsTable` (Shared) are used on both the agent's page and `/internal-agents`, which adds up the running totals and lists the latest requests of all agents. `RequestCount` is a concurrency token and the store retries when simultaneous requests collide. An unknown model is recorded with its tokens at no cost, and failing to record is logged and never breaks the agent. Copilot prompts are edited in `MarkdownEditor` (WYSIWYG, like every Markdown editor); background agent prompts stay plain text.
- Copilot chats: Web uses `AssistantChat` with a `CopilotKey` and tools from `AssistantForms.ForAgent` / `ForWorkItem` / `ForWorkItemTemplate`. Form tools read and update state through an `onUi` callback (`InvokeAsync` + `StateHasChanged`) and expose a form snapshot. Tools only change the form; the user saves. The work item chat agents have no section structure in their prompts: `WorkItemFormTools` sends the selected template and a copy of the current title and description along with every user message (`AssistantTools.RequestContext`) and offers `get_selected_template`; the template isn't stored on the item, so a saved draft has none selected. Replies are rendered as Markdown by `ChatMarkdown`, which treats model output as untrusted (prompt injection): raw HTML is escaped, only http(s)/mailto links are kept and images become links; keep it that way. The one exception is the chat page with the DGHSF Agent: its `ChatLog` sets `AppLinks`, which also keeps relative links to exactly the page of a work item or mindmap (`AppPaths.IsLinkablePage`), opened in the same tab, and turns a link to the GitHub issue of one of the repository's work items (`WorkItemIssueLinks`) into a link to that item's page. The agent's tools give every work item and mindmap its `page` path, and `ProjectAgentTools.LinkInstructions` (appended to the stored prompt on every conversation, so it isn't lost in a customized or older prompt) tells it to link those instead of GitHub. A disabled chat agent hides its chat. Before a conversation starts, `AssistantChat` asks the Chat Suggestions agent (`BackgroundAgents.SuggestPromptsAsync`, with the form snapshot) for 3 chips; the page's static suggestions are the fallback. On the work item editors the chips are written again (`AssistantChat.RefreshSuggestions`) when the title or description loses focus after a change (`MarkdownEditor.OnBlur`), not per keystroke; during a conversation no chips are shown, so nothing is refreshed.
- Background agents (`BackgroundAgents`) use structured output (`RunAsync<T>`), so edited prompts can't break the result format. `WorkItemModelSelector` lets the Model Selector suggest an enabled managed model for a story, bug or task (`WorkItemService.SelectModelAsync`; nothing is saved). The work item editor debounces it: 3 seconds after the last description change (typed or filled in by the Copilot) it shows the suggestion as a chip under the model picker, and clicking the chip applies it. It also suggests once, without delay, when an existing draft with a description is opened; other fields and new items (template skeletons) don't trigger it. The model is never picked automatically: "Auto" stays Copilot's automatic model selection.
- `MarkdownEditor` and `MarkdownViewer` create Toast UI editors and viewers in `MarkdownEditor.razor.js` through Toast UI's public API (contract covered by `MarkdownEditorTests`); the ToastUIEditor package is only used for the Toast UI script and stylesheet it ships (imported by path, so its version is pinned exactly), not for its Blazor components. The editor's `addImageBlobHook` replaces Toast UI's base64 images. With `AllowImages` (work item and work item template editors) and the `ImageUploads` config section set, images stream over the circuit to `ImageUploadService`, which validates the format by signature and stores them under a random name in a public Azure blob container (`IImageStorage`); otherwise images are refused.
- Title fields (work item title, template title example) are `DictationTextField`s: a `MudTextField` with a microphone end adornment (none when read-only). It is hidden unless the `Speech` config section (`SpeechOptions`: `Region`, `ApiKey`, optional `Endpoint`, `Language` with up to four comma-separated locales for language detection) is set. `SpeechService.GetTokenAsync` (MediatR `GetSpeechTokenQuery`) has `AzureSpeechTokenIssuer` exchange the key for a 10-minute Azure AI Speech token, reused until 2 minutes before it expires. `wwwroot/js/dictation.js` then recognizes one utterance in the browser with the Speech SDK for JavaScript, which is vendored in `wwwroot/lib/microsoft-cognitiveservices-speech-sdk-<version>` (the path has the version; update it with the files). The key never goes to the browser. The text is trimmed and loses its closing period before it replaces the field.
- Description editors (work item description, template skeleton) pass a `DescriptionDictation` to `MarkdownEditor`, which then shows a microphone at the top right, next to its `Header` (the pages pass their heading and help text). It listens continuously (`recognizeContinuous` in `dictation.js`, with interim text shown under the editor and the token renewed every minute through `GetSpeechToken`) until the microphone is clicked again or Done, at most 10 minutes. `SpeechService.WriteDescriptionAsync` (MediatR `WriteDictatedDescriptionQuery`) then lets the Description Writer background agent merge the transcript into the current description, following the template skeleton; when that agent is disabled, unconfigured or fails, the transcript is appended as a new paragraph. The result replaces the description, with Undo in the snackbar.
- Work item templates have an `IsDefault` flag: at most one per type, because `WorkItemTemplateStore.SaveAsync` clears the previous default in the same save. `WorkItemTemplate.Proposed` picks the default, or else the first alphabetically; new items and generated children both use it.
- Child generation: `WorkItemTypeRules.GeneratedChildType` maps epic to feature, feature to story and story to task. The editor's Generate button (bottom of the page, in the children box; hidden when the Work Item Breakdown agent is disabled or not configured) saves the item and opens `WorkItemChildGenerator` (`/{plural}/{id}/generate`). That page runs the agent (`BackgroundAgents.GenerateChildrenAsync`, MediatR `GenerateChildWorkItemsQuery`) with the parent, the proposed template and the existing children's titles; nothing is stored. The selected proposals are saved as drafts in one transaction (`SaveGeneratedWorkItemsCommand`, `IWorkItemStore.AddGeneratedChildrenAsync`). The agent's output is cleaned in `BackgroundAgents` (blank and duplicate titles dropped, lengths and `GeneratedWorkItem.MaxPerRun` enforced).
- Write extension methods with C# 14 `extension(...)` blocks.
- Use block bodies (`{ ... }`) for methods, constructors, operators and local functions, also in Razor `@code` blocks; expression bodies only where a block is not possible. `.editorconfig` enforces this for C# files.
- UI pages are Razor components using MudBlazor. Tests use xUnit and bUnit in `tests\Djohnnie.SoftwareFactory.Web.Tests`.
- `AppNavigation` doesn't link template pages: each work item list page has a Templates button right after its New button, and the agents page links the agent templates (From template). The template pages and their editors have that list page in their breadcrumbs (e.g. Overview > Epics > Epic templates).
- Every page in the main layout starts with `PageBreadcrumbs`: the trail from the overview and a back arrow to the page one level up (`BackHref` overrides it). Page actions go in a row of text buttons between the title and the first box, as on the overview pages; detail pages have no Cancel, because the back arrow does that. Pages editing something stored have a Reset that confirms, loads the stored version again without setting `_loading` (which would tear down the form and its Copilot conversation), and isn't shown on new items.

## Repository guidance

`README.md` describes the app, local setup (settings, tests) and deployment for people; this file holds the details for Copilot. `IDEAS.md` includes both implemented features and roadmap items; confirm behavior in the source before treating planned features as available.
